explain.say: Phytoplankton are microscopic algae and bacteria that photosynthesise in sunlit surface water. They need sunlight from above and nutrients like nitrate and iron, which are richest where cold water wells up from the deep.

faq.q: What is the difference between phytoplankton and zooplankton?
faq.a: Phytoplankton are plant-like: tiny algae and bacteria that make food from sunlight. Zooplankton are animals, from tiny copepods and krill to fish larvae and jellyfish, that eat phytoplankton or each other.
asks: What are the two types of plankton?
Is plankton a plant or an animal?

faq.q: Does plankton make the oxygen we breathe?
faq.a: A lot of it. Ocean phytoplankton carry out roughly half of the photosynthesis on Earth, so they release a huge share of the oxygen in the air, alongside land plants.
asks: Where does Earth's oxygen come from?

faq.q: What is the biggest migration on Earth?
faq.a: Every night, vast numbers of zooplankton and small fish rise from the dark depths to feed near the surface and sink again by dawn. By the number of animals involved, it is thought to be the biggest migration on Earth.
asks: Why does plankton move up at night?

faq.a: No. Plankton means drifter, so anything that drifts with currents counts, including jellyfish, some of which have tentacles many metres long. Most plankton, though, are too small to see without a microscope.

When light and nutrients are plentiful, often in spring, phytoplankton multiply so fast that they colour the sea green or turquoise, and the blooms can be seen from space. They feed a burst of ocean life.
asks: Why does the sea turn green?
Can you see plankton from space?

facts: Marine phytoplankton carry out roughly half of the photosynthesis on Earth.
The daily up-and-down movement of zooplankton is often described as the largest migration on Earth.
